clue.text: Sweet spoils hero may initially grant

parts.note: to spoil is to mar, so 'spoils' is MARS

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letters of the two words just before it

parts.note: to grant is to allow

explanation.surface: A conquering hero might hand out the spoils of victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'hero' and 'may', giving H and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshmallow is a soft spongy confection, an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Crazy morning, yes?

parts.note: AM is the usual abbreviation for morning (ante meridiem)
OK is an informal yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it has been a mad morning.
explanation.definitionFit: To run amok is to go berserk, so the word describes crazed, frenzied behaviour.

clue.text: Son's on notice, with head getting grief

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed on another sits above it, so the son comes first

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son; the 's stands for 'is'
an ad is a notice or advertisement
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A son has been given notice and his chief is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief and sadness are both words for sorrow.

clue.text: Powder in very small measure

definitions.meaning: to grind into powder, so it is a verb meaning to powder
a thousandth of a dollar, a tiny unit used in tax rates

explanation.surface: A drug dose in a tiny quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinding grain into flour is milling it; separately, a mill is a money unit worth one tenth of a cent.

clue.text: Seek frantically after facilities for gander

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes after the toilet in the answer

parts.note: facilities is a euphemism for toilets, and a loo is a toilet

indicators.note: done frantically the letters are thrown about wildly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone desperately searching for the toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' is not the male goose but the informal noun for a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A gander and a look-see are both slang for a quick glance at something.

clue.text: Listen! You could be putting on weight!

indicators.note: the weight is putting on the pronoun like a garment, so it goes around it

parts.note: OZ is the abbreviation for ounce, a weight
YE is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A warning that someone may be gaining weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' is only a link: 'putting on' pictures the weight wearing the old pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Oyez is the town crier's call for silence and attention, meaning hear ye.

clue.text: Drink flexibly — it's essential for life

parts.note: water is a drink
supply is an adverb form of supple, meaning flexibly

explanation.surface: Advice to drink in a relaxed way, since it keeps you alive.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPPLY here is supple + -ly, not the noun meaning stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A water supply provides what every living thing depends on to survive.

clue.text: Depression, daughter admitted, can be merciless

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between mountain peaks
blooded means initiated, admitted into a group by a first experience

explanation.surface: A daughter's depression could make her hard-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' is not low spirits but a dip between peaks; 'admitted' is BLOODED, as a novice is blooded.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold-blooded describes cruelty without feeling or pity.

clue.text: Get this straight — accept I'm old and confused!

indicators.note: getting something straight means sorting it out, so these letters are put in order

explanation.surface: An old person admitting to muddled thinking and asking to be set right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something confused is tangled and intricate, which is what complicated means.

clue.text: Shabby lad I titivated with very good old hat

indicators.note: titivated means smartened up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: PI, short for pious, means very good
old hat means out of date, dated

explanation.surface: A shabby lad got spruced up with a fine old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'titivated' rearranges LADI into DILA. PI for pious is crosswordese for very good.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilapidated means run-down and in disrepair, much like worn or shabby.

clue.text: Deterioration in sport — consequently a drop

parts.note: to sport clothes is to wear them
and can mean and so, introducing a consequence
a tear is a drop from the eye

explanation.surface: A sporting decline leads to a tearful moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear and tear is the gradual damage caused by everyday use, a form of decline.

clue.text: Skunk consuming some tomato ketchup

indicators.note: the phrase consumes, or holds, some of its letters, so the answer is hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A skunk eating some tomato ketchup.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Skunk consuming' is not a noun; the skunk alone is the definition and 'consuming some' signals the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Atok is a name for a South American skunk, a crossword-only word.

clue.text: Periodical laziness girl's shrugged off

indicators.note: letters shrugged off are cast aside, so they are removed from the word

parts.note: a lass is a girl; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A girl casting off her laziness.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LASS are removed from LAZINESS in order (LA at the start, SS at the end).
explanation.definitionFit: A zine is a small self-published magazine, a type of periodical.

clue.text: Train voice

explanation.surface: A singing instruction: train your voice.
explanation.definitionFit: An express is a fast service train; expressing a view means putting it into words.

clue.text: Hotchpotch of pitiful housing left uninhabited in centre

indicators.note: one word housing another holds it inside

parts.note: pitiful means sad

indicators.note: the centre letter of the eleven-letter word is taken

explanation.surface: A miserable dwelling left empty in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in centre' takes A, the sixth of the eleven letters of 'uninhabited'; LA goes inside SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad can mean a jumbled mixture, as a hotchpotch is.

clue.text: Fabulous creature sappers in the end disinterred, retaining name: 'Fabulous Creature'

indicators.note: the reworked creature retains, or holds within it, the extra letter
fabulous here means fanciful, invented, so the word is reworked into a new arrangement
disinterred means dug out, and in the end points to the last pair of letters being removed

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are sappers

explanation.surface: Army engineers finally dig up a mythical beast and give it a name.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the final RE from CREATURE leaves CREATU; 'Fabulous' rearranges it to CETAUR, which retains N inside. The quoted words deliberately repeat the definition as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur is a mythical half-man, half-horse, a creature of fable.

clue.text: Equal rises to Charlie and Inch

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a peer is an equal

explanation.surface: A capitalised name list: something rising to Charlie and Inch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns PEER into REEP, placed below C. 'Inch' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch and to creep both mean to move forward very slowly.

clue.text: Weapon oddly scabbarded

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in the odd positions of the word

explanation.surface: A weapon has been sheathed in a strange way.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabre is a curved cavalry sword, a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Container captain's caper

definitions.meaning: a large open waste container, as used by builders in Britain
short for skipper, a team captain; the 's stands for 'is'
to caper, to leap about playfully

explanation.surface: A ship captain's escapade involving a shipping container.
explanation.definitionFit: A British skip is a builder's dumpster; a skip is a team captain; skipping is lively hopping.

clue.text: Mark's wrong to accept Young's tip

indicators.note: one word accepting another takes it inside

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: the tip here is the end letter of the word

explanation.surface: A mark that it was wrong to take a tip from Young.
explanation.walkthrough: The tip of 'Young' is its last letter G, which goes inside SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a mark or symbol indicating something.

clue.text: This plus insect flying around provokes apprentices daily

indicators.note: letters flying around are scattered, so the combined letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A buzzing insect is irritating young trainees.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer ('This') plus INSECT can be rearranged to spell APPRENTICES, a composite anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a newspaper published every day, which is a paper.

clue.text: Shot captures Ruby, first to tender bet

indicators.note: one word capturing another holds it inside

parts.note: a pic is a photograph, a shot
ruby is a shade of red

indicators.note: first to takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A gunshot hits a ruby, prompting a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bet' is the verb, as in 'I bet it rains'; 'Shot' is a photograph, not gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: To bet that something will happen is to predict it.

clue.text: Rearing sheep, Dad closes in sylvan tract

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
Pa is dad

indicators.note: closes are ends, so the last letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A father raising sheep in a woodland area.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant in heraldry describes an animal reared up on its hind legs.

clue.text: Quietly embellish account within advert

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: the account goes within the other word

parts.note: to lard a speech is to embellish it

explanation.surface: Discreetly padding a figure in an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a poster or sign put up for public notice, an advertisement.

clue.text: Spectacle cases years in long …

indicators.note: one word casing another wraps around it

parts.note: to long for is to pant for
an age is many years

explanation.surface: A show that has been running for years, its sentence finished in the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a grand public show or procession.

clue.text: … fabricated cover lined with ermine's tail

indicators.note: a cover lined with something has it inside

parts.note: a lid is a cover

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the show invented a story about a cover with ermine trim.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail of 'ermine' is E, placed inside LID.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabricated means made up, as a story that is lied.

clue.text: Stripped-down comedy coming up in March, perhaps?

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming up means reading from bottom to top
stripped down means the outer letters are taken away, leaving the inside

explanation.surface: A minimalist comedy show opening in the spring month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripped-down' leaves OMED; 'coming up' turns it to read DEMO. 'March' is a protest march, not the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a public demonstration, a protest march being one example.

clue.text: Second-class in tube train leaving Turin

indicators.note: the letters of the city are leaving, so they are removed

explanation.surface: Second-class seats on a metro train departing from Turin.
explanation.walkthrough: T, U, R, I, N are taken out of TUBETRAIN in order, leaving BETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, used as a grade below alpha.

clue.text: Girl backing article by parson

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a parson

explanation.surface: A girl supports an article written by a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a female first name, so it fits the crossword convention of 'girl' standing for any woman's name.

clue.text: Leading light from Brussels area?

parts.note: Brussels sprouts are veg

explanation.surface: A prominent figure from around the Belgian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Brussels is not the city but the sprout, a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is one of the brightest stars in the night sky, a literal leading light.

clue.text: Took counsel when brought back to gaol?

definitions.meaning: to deliberate is to consider carefully and discuss
read as ..., the opposite of freed, so returned to prison

explanation.surface: A prisoner who sought legal advice after being returned to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberating is weighing a matter with care; whimsically, undoing liberation means locking someone up again.

clue.text: Set out urn and teapot, Ma, in case

indicators.note: letters set out are laid out afresh, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mother unpacks the urn and teapot from a travelling case.
explanation.definitionFit: A portmanteau is a large travelling bag or suitcase.
